title: Collection expressions
hook: C# 12 replaced new List<int> { 1, 2, 3 } noise with [1, 2, 3] and spread .. . They always materialize. They are not a third kind of LINQ.

sections.heading: Syntax and targets
sections.prose: A collection expression is a bracketed list of elements. The compiler converts it to an array, List<T>, Span<T>, ImmutableArray<T>, or any type with a collection initializer or a CollectionBuilderAttribute. You can pass [1, 2, 3] as an argument. You cannot use one as a default parameter or a const. The empty form [] can become Array.Empty<T>() when the target will not be mutated. Spread ..enumerable inlines elements. Microsoft warns: conversion to IEnumerable<T> still allocates an in-memory collection of every element — unlike a yield iterator or a LINQ Select.

snippets.label: Batch ids and a spread
snippets.explanation: Spreads copy elements into a new list. with(...) constructor arguments on collection expressions are a later C# addition; C# 12 introduced the brackets and spread. Prefer Ordinal comparers for ids.

sections.heading: Overload resolution and Span
sections.prose: A collection expression converts to many types, so overloaded APIs may need a cast. Conversion to Span / ReadOnlySpan / other ref structs is preferred over heap collections; conversion to a concrete type is preferred over an interface. That is why some BCL methods grew Span overloads. Storing the result as Span still follows ref-struct rules (module 17).

sections.heading: What not to do
sections.prose: Do not replace a streaming CSV yield with a collection expression of all rows. Do not assume IEnumerable<T> x = [.. huge]; is lazy. Do not use collection expressions to build infinite sequences — they cannot. For a tiny allow-list of auth scopes, ["exam.write", "exam.read"] is the right default in C# 14 / .NET 10 code.

interviewTakeaways: Introduced in C# 12; [e1, e2, ..rest] is the syntax.
Always eager; IEnumerable<T> target still allocates.
Can target arrays, List, Span, immutable collections, and builder-attributed types.
commonPitfalls: Thinking [..query] is as lazy as query.
Using collection expressions as default parameter values (illegal).
Ambiguous overloads when both List and Span are applicable without a cast.

jsTsCorrelations.note: [...a, ...b] in JS always makes a new Array. C# [..a, ..b] makes whatever the target type is.
TS as const freezes literal types. C# collection expressions pick a BCL collection type from context, not a tuple type unless you target a tuple.
